description: ADMISSION on the OSF registration TEMPLATE. The registrant 10.17605 covers 25,819 pool rows, 3,016 of them with no abstract at all, and 21 known FLoRA papers are on it — so neither the registrant nor the missing abstract may discard (measured 2026-08-04; rule_ideas.md SS2b). What separates the rows is the template the registration was filed under, which OSF exposes as `attributes.registration_supplement` and which `filter/engine/backfill.py` now writes as the FIRST LINE of the overlay text: `OSF registration template: <name>`. A spec cannot call an API at routing time, so the template arrives as text and this rule reads it off the anchored first line — that anchor, and the string in `search/fetch_abstracts.py::OSF_TEMPLATE_PREFIX` that produces it, are one contract, and changing either without the other is a routing change. TWO ARMS, and they ask for different amounts because the templates say different amounts. A POST-COMPLETION template — in practice `Replication Recipe (Brandt et al., 2013): Post-Completion` — is a report of a finished study: the record states its outcome in the Replication Recipe's own vocabulary, one sampled registration giving `d = 0.06`, `CI = [-.218, .340]` and `item33: "informative failure to replicate"`, which is what Stage 3 exists to extract and here arrives without a PDF or a title search. That template is admitted on its own, with no phrase requirement. `Open-Ended Registration` is a content-free container — it says only that something was registered — so it is admitted only when the record's own text also carries the replication stem, which is the maintainer's ruling of 2026-08-04 with the intent marker the ruling implies. WHERE THAT STEM ACTUALLY FIRES, measured over the full population: the TITLE, in 99% of the 336 rows this arm admits, not the responses form. The arm reaches almost exactly one thing — Reproducibility Project: Psychology registrations, titled "Replication of Janiszewski & Uy (2008, PS, Study 4b)" and carrying "Registered prior to RPP publication" as their entire text. That is a fair use of the record's own words and the arm works, but it is title matching, and an Open-Ended registration whose replication evidence is buried in a long responses form is not what this arm is reaching. An open scope question sits underneath it: for an individual RPP study the OSF registration may be the only record that exists. `post[-\s]?completion` is the whole of the first arm: OSF's `Post-Data Collection` forms are NOT covered, on the maintainer's ruling of 2026-08-04 that a post-data-collection registration is still a registration of a design and not a report of results, and no known FLoRA paper sits on one. If a template fetch over the full no-abstract population ever finds a FLoRA paper on such a form, that finding — not the naming — is what reopens the arm. The stem arm is `replicat*` only — reproduction vocabulary is #155's stream and is not admitted here on the strength of an OSF sample of four. Precedence 936 sits ABOVE this rule's discard twin `osf-registration-protocol` (935) and above the whole admission band, and BELOW the definitional discards (940-960) which say the record is not a paper at all. Above the 700s because for an overlay row the template line is a better statement of what the record IS than any phrase in the responses text it precedes — a preregistration's responses are full of `we will replicate Smith (2009)` and would otherwise be admitted by `replication-claim-text` (730). Above the twin by exactly one because the two match blocks are hand-synced copies with no way for a spec to reference another: if they ever drift, the row is kept and screened rather than deleted, which is the cheaper of the two errors. `tests/test_osf_registrations.py` asserts the partition, and is the guard the format cannot give. `vocabulary` is null: an admission to the two-voter screen is a request for attention, not a verdict that the record is a replication (CONVENTIONS.md, "Pile -> filter_status"). Fires on nothing until a backfill has run: the first line it matches exists only in overlay text this project wrote.

measured.sample: The whole no-abstract population on registrant 10.17605 — 3,016 rows of 25,819 on the registrant, counted on disk; templates fetched for all of them 2026-08-04, 1,674 resolving to registrations. Each row put through this spec by eval_spec_rows(). Artifacts: analysis/osf_registrations/{REPORT.md, census.csv}.
measured.rationale: An admission rule needs no evidence to run (CONVENTIONS.md, promotion note 4) — the worst it does is buy a screen call — so this entry records what the arms reach rather than satisfying a gate. It admits 366 rows: 30 Post-Completion (holding all four known FLoRA Post-Completion registrations) and 336 Open-Ended carrying the replication stem, which are overwhelmingly RPP registrations matched on their title. 49 of those 336 are known FLoRA records outright against the flora.csv regenerated 2026-08-05 — the OSF registration DOIs were added to the COS source sheet that day — so what this arm admits is demonstrably a second record for replications FLoRA already holds, and Stage 3's skip list drops them with nothing further built. Whether the individual RPP registration is a record in its own right is a scope call for the maintainer, not a rule question. No post-completion template other than the Replication Recipe's appeared anywhere in the population, and no post-DATA-COLLECTION template appeared at all — so the keep arm dropped on the maintainer's 2026-08-04 ruling cost nothing, which is now a count rather than an argument. What this does NOT support: any precision claim about the 366, none of which was read. Eleven further known FLoRA rows in the population are OSF projects rather than registrations, get no text, and are reached by neither rule; they stay pending/no_text. The population's known-FLoRA count is 64 in total and will keep moving as identifiers are added to FLoRA — read it as a denominator that grows, not as a fact about these rows.
